messages.content: Why are puddles gone much faster on a sunny afternoon than on a cloudy one?
The sun dries them faster. Because sunshine warms the water, and warm water evaporates into the air more quickly than cool water.
Why does a steel nail sink while a huge steel ship floats?

The ship's shape lets it push aside a lot of water. Because a hollow, wide ship pushes aside a weight of water greater than its own, so the water holds it up, while a small solid nail pushes aside too little.
Why might someone feel nervous about speaking in front of the class, even when they know the topic well?
Speaking to a crowd feels risky. Because they worry about forgetting words or being judged, and that worry makes the heart race even when they are well prepared.
Why does a plant on a windowsill bend towards the window?
It is reaching for light. Because plants need light to make food, and the stem grows faster on the shaded side, which tips the top towards the brighter side.
Why do rooms feel warmer when many people are inside?
Each person gives off heat. Because our bodies make warmth all the time, and in a closed room it adds up with nowhere to go.
I have a test tomorrow and a game tonight. How can I decide what to do?
Think about which matters more and whether both are possible. Because you may be able to study first and play later, and weighing the two helps you avoid regrets.
Why does soap clean greasy hands better than water alone?
Soap grabs grease and water together. Because each soap particle has a grease-loving end and a water-loving end, the grease is lifted off the skin and carried away when you rinse.
Why should we leave a little spare time between two tasks in our day?
A gap soaks up delays. Because tasks often take longer than we expect, a gap stops a delay from spoiling everything that comes next.
Why do people check the weather report before planning a picnic?
They check the report so the picnic is not ruined. Because rain or strong heat would make the day unpleasant, knowing in advance lets them pick a better day.
Why does a snake keep flicking its tongue in and out?

The snake flicks its tongue to smell its surroundings. Because the tongue picks up tiny particles from the air and the ground and brings them to special organs in the mouth, the snake can find food and sense danger.
Why is it a good idea to look at a route before cycling to a new place?
Looking at the route first saves trouble. Because it helps us avoid wrong turns and very busy roads, we reach the place with less stress and more safely.
Why should a pot on the stove never be left alone for long?

Things can go wrong quickly on a stove, so someone should stay nearby. Because food can boil over onto the flame or boil dry and burn, and a fire can start when nobody is there to stop it, a pot should not be left alone.
Why do shadows grow long in the late afternoon?

A low sun throws long shadows. Because light from a low sun reaches objects at a slant, it stretches their shadows far across the ground, while from high overhead it falls almost straight down and the shadow stays short.
Why do farmers choose seeds to match the season?
Seeds need the right weather to grow. Because a crop planted in the wrong season may face cold, drought or flood, matching it to the season gives it the best chance.
Why are green mangoes sour and ripe mangoes sweet?
Ripening turns acids and starch into sugars. Because the fruit changes its chemicals as it matures on the tree or in the store, the sourness fades and the sweetness grows.
Why does a room with no furniture sound echoey?
Sound bounces around the bare room. Because hard walls and floors send the sound back instead of soaking it up, the reflections reach our ears a little after the original voice.
Mother cuts 48 guavas equally for 8 children. How many does each child get?
6. Because 8 x 6 = 48, so each one gets 6 with none left over.
Find the sum of 84 and 95.
179. Because 84 + 95 = 179, adding the tens first and then the ones.
What is 28 + 32?
60. Because 28 + 32 = 60, adding the tens first and then the ones.
Priya is 35 years old and her brother is 10 years older. How old is the brother?
45. Because 35 + 10 = 45, so the brother is 45 years old.
